title: Bijectivity of units-stalk evaluation in an algebraically closed overfield
statement: Let $K$ be a field, $K^s$ its separable closure, and $\Omega$ an algebraically closed overfield containing $K^s$ in a compatible $K$-tower [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pd-separable-closure]. Let $p$ be the geometric point of $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and $\mathbf G_m$ its additive units sheaf [def-sc-gm-torsor]. Every additive map $f:(\mathbf G_m)_p\to\operatorname{Additive}((K^s)^\times)$ satisfying $i(f(\operatorname{germ}_x z))=\Gamma\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega)(x^*z)$ on every germ is bijective; the formula uses the values of units, removes the ULift by down, and uses the canonical global-sections isomorphism. No equivariance hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Use joint surjectivity of the filtered-colimit germ maps to represent two stalk elements on one neighbourhood X. At the image y of the chosen lift, the base residue-field spectrum is isomorphic to Spec K because it is a reduced surjective closed immersion. The source etale residue-field map theorem then makes Spec kappa(y) -> X -> Spec K etale. Factor the lift through this new neighbourhood. Its residue-field embedding into Omega is injective. Global-sections naturality makes equal evaluations imply equal restricted units. The filtered-colimit equality criterion identifies the two original germs.

For a desired unit a, take the finite separable simple intermediate field K(a) in Ks. Its spectrum is etale. Its inclusion followed by Ks -> Omega gives a pointed neighbourhood. The unit a in this field, transported through the inverse global-sections isomorphism, defines a section and germ. Evaluation naturality and injectivity of Ks -> Omega identify its image with a, proving surjectivity.
